questions.question: If you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test, what happens?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
You get an extra point against your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When you exit your vehicle during the test, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact with it at all times. On a bus, you must hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you fail the entire test.

questions.question: When dropping off students at school, what should the driver do?

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students are getting off at school, turn off the engine to secure the bus. If you leave your seat, remove the key from the ignition. You must watch the students while they unload.

questions.question: When picking up students, you must make sure all traffic has stopped before doing what?

options.text: Opening the door and calling students to approach.
Turning on the flashing red lights.
Pulling over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening the door and calling students to approach.
questions.explanation: Before you open the door and signal students to come to the bus, all surrounding traffic must have come to a complete stop.

questions.question: If a student may have a back injury, what should you do?

options.text: Move them off the bus.
Do not move them.
Help them try to stand up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them.
questions.explanation: Never move a student who may have a neck or spine injury. Only move them if their life is in immediate danger.

questions.question: Before driving, what should you check about the pedals?

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The grooved surface of the pedals is not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved surface of the pedals is not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that could block them. Make sure the pedals work properly and that grooved pedal surfaces have not worn smooth.

questions.question: What is a passive railroad crossing?

options.text: A crossing with a control device.
A crossing with no control devices.
A crossing that should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossing with no control devices.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no traffic control devices like lights or gates. The driver must decide whether it is safe to cross.

questions.question: Who can change bus stops?

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: The school district sets all official bus routes and stops. Drivers must never change a stop without written permission from a district official.

questions.question: Do school buses have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They never have ABS.
They only have ABS in cold climates.
They may have ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may have ABS.
questions.explanation: Most commercial vehicles made after 1998 or 1999 must have ABS. Many older buses also have ABS.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery surfaces.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the brakes from locking up on slippery roads. This helps you maintain control when braking hard on wet or icy surfaces. Drive and brake the same way whether your bus has ABS or not.

questions.question: If there is a fire on a school bus, what must happen to the students?

options.text: They must get off the bus.
They should stay on the bus and move away from the fire.
They should stay in their seats.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must get off the bus.
questions.explanation: If there is a fire on the bus or a risk of fire, you must evacuate all students immediately.

questions.question: When inspecting a fifth wheel before a trip, what should you check?

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel locking jaws must be completely closed around the kingpin shaft. This keeps the trailer safely connected.

questions.question: What should you do if students on the bus cause trouble while other students are getting off?

options.text: Immediately go to the back of the bus and handle the problem while students unload.
Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the problem.
Ask a nearby student to handle it while you watch the unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are off the bus, then handle the problem.
questions.explanation: You must focus completely on loading and unloading students. Wait until all students have safely exited before dealing with behavior problems.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go back up after a train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to check if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If a gate stays down after a train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, first pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: How should students safely get off the bus?

options.text: Stay seated until told to exit.
Stand up and move toward the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit the bus and stand next to it while the bus is being driven away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until told to exit.
questions.explanation: Students must stay seated until the driver tells them to exit. After leaving the bus, they should walk at least 10 feet away so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: Backing up a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only done in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Backing a school bus should be avoided whenever possible. Only back up if there is no other safe option. Always follow proper safety steps.

questions.question: During the driving test, what should you do when asked to change lanes?

options.text: Do not worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes during the driving test, check your surroundings, use your turn signal, and smoothly move into the new lane when safe.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: When a driver misses their basic skills test.
When a vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
When a driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment occurs when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during a basic skills test exercise. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: Where should students stay during an emergency?

options.text: On the bus
On the side of the road near the bus
In a field away from the bus

questions.correctAnswerText: On the bus
questions.explanation: In most emergencies, students are safer and easier to control on the bus. Only evacuate students if staying on the bus puts them at risk.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them differently each time to check different items.
Do them the same way each time to avoid forgetting anything.
Do them occasionally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time to avoid forgetting anything.
questions.explanation: Use the same inspection process before every trip. This helps you remember all steps and makes sure nothing is missed.
